title: Fuzzy deprioritization scheduler for KV contention and SLO-preserving fairness
creator: Claire Zhang
description:
Problem: under continuous batching we see pathological cases where a minority of tenants with large working sets repeatedly evict KV cache pages and induce preemption storms that inflate p95/p99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants. Existing strict priority preemptors either starve noisy tenants or cause oscillation when KV pressure fluctuates.

Goal: implement a scheduler that preserves SLOs for latency-tiered tenants while allowing best-effort throughput. The design must:
- reduce KV eviction churn by probabilistically deprioritizing requests contributing most to KV pressure,
- ensure no-tenant starvation via credit accumulation windows,
- be compatible with continuous batching (does not block batch formation) and GPU memory accounting,
- expose tuning knobs for per-tenant SLO slack, token budgets, and soft/hard KV reservations.

Proposal (high level): a "fuzzy deprioritization" scoring model: each request is assigned a deprio_score = alpha*kv_pressure_est + beta*latency_slack_norm - gamma*tenant_credit. Values are normalized to 0..1. Requests with deprio_score above a dynamic threshold are labeled "deprioritized" and their admission probability is reduced by p = exp(-lambda * deprio_score). Deprioritized requests still join batches but are placed into later admission slices; they may be preempted last. The scheduler maintains tenant_credit that accrues when tenant requests are delayed and decays slowly. KV_pressure_est uses an exponentially weighted moving average of misses per second and estimated bytes evicted if admitted.

Trade-offs: increases scheduler complexity and tuning surface; probabilistic decisions may add variance but avoid global thrashing. We accept slight throughput loss for improved p95 for latency-tier tenants.

Implementation plan:
1) Add lightweight KV pressure estimator in the runtime metrics layer (C++/Go shim) emitting per-tenant kv_miss_rate and estimated_eviction_bytes.
2) Implement scoring function and probabilistic admission in the batch admission module (Go scheduler).
3) Integrate tenant_credit store persisted in memtable with eviction-safe semantics.
4) Add feature flags and per-tenant configs (slo_slack, token_budget, kv_soft_reservation).
5) Unit tests + microbench harness to simulate mixed working sets.
6) Staged canary: 5% of nodes with canary config, telemetry to new dashboard panels.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- p95 latency for latency-tier tenants improves by >=15% under mixed-load KV-contended benchmark,
- KV eviction rate (evicted bytes / admitted bytes) reduces by >=20% under the same benchmark,
- No tenant is starved: 99.9% of requests see progress within 2x their SLA window,
- Feature has a runtime toggle and per-tenant opt-in.

Rollout plan: experimental canary (runtime-1.19.alpha) -> gated rollout to runtime-1.19 after 2 weeks of stable metrics -> enable by default for best-effort tenants in runtime-1.19.

comments: 2026-01-25 - Claire Zhang: Initial RFC uploaded to Confluence; added baseline microbench results showing 30% eviction churn for benchmark mix.

2026-02-03 - Rohit Gupta: Reviewed scoring formula. Suggest replacing linear tenant_credit subtraction with a bounded logistic transform to avoid negative scores; also requested that deprioritized requests still be eligible for batching to preserve throughput.
2026-02-12 - Miguel Santos: Implemented KV pressure estimator prototype (PR #5842). Local sim shows deprio reduces eviction rate by ~18% but increases p50 by ~5ms. Pushed more granular telemetry.

2026-02-27 - Aisha Kapoor: Design review notes - ensure GPU memory accounting includes temporary KV page pinning during attention recompute. Also asked for a safe fallthrough to strict preemptor under extreme memory pressure.
2026-03-05 - Claire Zhang: Integrated feature flag and per-tenant config, added canary deployment script. Created dashboard panels to track deprio_score distribution and admitted_probability.
2026-03-10 - QA: Canary run (48h) summary: p95 improved 17% for latency-tier, eviction bytes down 22%. Observed two tenants with long-tail retries — fixed by increasing credit accumulation rate.
